title: Accessibility basics in React
summary: Semantic HTML first, labels and accessible names, keyboard support and focus, ARIA attributes in JSX, live regions, and checking accessibility in tests.

sections.title: Semantic HTML first
sections.body:
Use the element that already has the behaviour: `<button>` for actions (focusable, Enter and Space work, announced as a button), `<a href>` for navigation, `<label>` for form fields, headings in order, lists for lists. A `<div onClick>` is not focusable and not announced; making it accessible needs `role`, `tabIndex` and key handlers, so use a button instead.

In JSX, write `htmlFor` on labels; `aria-*` attributes keep their dashes and lower case: `aria-label`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-describedby`.
sections.code: We never share it.

sections.title: Names, states and IDs
sections.body:
Every control needs an **accessible name**: visible label text, `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby`. Icon-only buttons need `aria-label`. Images need `alt`; decorative images use `alt=""`.

Expose state with ARIA: `aria-expanded` on disclosure buttons, `aria-pressed` on toggle buttons, `aria-selected` on tabs, `aria-current="page"` on the current link. Use `useId()` to generate unique ids for linking labels and descriptions, so a component can be rendered several times without clashes.

sections.title: Keyboard and focus
sections.body:
Everything clickable must work with the keyboard and show a visible focus outline. Composite widgets such as tabs and menus follow the ARIA Authoring Practices: the tab list is one Tab stop, arrow keys move between tabs (roving `tabIndex`: 0 on the selected tab, -1 on others), and the selected tab controls a `role="tabpanel"`.

Manage focus when content changes: move focus into a dialog when it opens and back to the trigger when it closes, and move focus to the new heading after client-side navigation. Use refs for this.

sections.title: Announcements and testing
sections.body:
Status messages that appear without a focus change should be in a **live region**: `role="status"` (polite) or `role="alert"` (assertive, for errors). The region should exist before its text changes.

Testing by role and name (`getByRole("button", { name: "Save" })`) fails when names are missing, so accessible tests catch many a11y bugs. Add automated checks such as axe, and test with a keyboard and a screen reader.

pitfalls: Inputs without labels, or placeholders used as labels.
Hard-coded ids that clash when a component renders twice; use `useId`.
Removing focus outlines without a replacement.

gotchas.question: How do you write the HTML `for` attribute in JSX?
gotchas.answer: `htmlFor`, because `for` is a reserved word in JavaScript.

gotchas.question: Which role should a message that appears after a failed save use?
gotchas.answer: `role="alert"`, which announces assertively. Use `role="status"` for non-urgent updates.

gotchas.question: Why use `useId` instead of `id="name-input"`?
gotchas.answer: A hard-coded id is duplicated if the component renders twice, breaking label associations. `useId` produces a unique, stable id per instance (and matches between server and client).
